question: What does a geometric-mean reporting comment require for comparison of individual monitoring-period values?

row.DMR_COMMENT_TEXT: TOTAL DISSOLVED SOLIDS (TDS) MEASURED AT OUTFALL 001.  REPORT THE GEOMETRIC MEAN VALUE OF THE WEEKLY VALUES.

judgment.semantic_question_used: Does this permit limit row require reporting a geometric mean aggregate of weekly sample values (rather than, or in addition to, the period-level reported value) for monitoring or compliance evaluation?
judgment.interpretation: The structured DMR comment on this row repeats footnote *6 language about Total Dissolved Solids geometric-mean reporting, but the authoritative permit assigns that instruction only to the Total Dissolved Solids, Discharge (*6) pollutant row. This occurrence is BOD5 (parameter 00310) with a 30-day average mass-loading limit of 1669 lb/day (Q1, statistical base 3C). Part I of permit NM0020583 sets BOD5 limits at 1669 lb/day (30-day avg) and 2504 lb/day (7-day avg), with monitoring at 5/week per footnote *1 and 12-hour composite sampling—no geometric-mean reporting instruction. The geometric-mean-of-weekly-values requirement does not apply to this BOD5 limit row.
judgment.grounding: Permit NM0020583 Part I table distinguishes BOD5 (5/Week *1, numeric 30-day and 7-day mass limits) from Total Dissolved Solids, Discharge (*6), whose footnote *6 states: 'Total dissolved solids measured at Outfall 001. Report the geometric mean value of weekly values.' The occurrence row identifies PARAMETER_CODE 00310 (BOD, 5-day) and LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR 1669 lb/d Q1. Statement of basis confirms BOD5/TSS are monitored five times per week on at least five different days with 12-hour composite samples, while TDS has separate once-per-week reporting requirements.

judgment.remaining_uncertainty: The limit-set-level DMR_COMMENT_TEXT in permit_limits.csv propagates the TDS footnote *6 text to all parameters sharing LIMIT_SET_ID 3600645646, including BOD; permit narrative text resolves this mismatch for this occurrence, but the structured comment field alone would be misleading without the permit document.
